source.text: זֶ֣ה סֵ֔פֶר תּוֹלְדֹ֖ת אָדָ֑ם בְּי֗וֹם בְּרֹ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אָדָ֔ם בִּדְמ֥וּת אֱלֹהִ֖ים עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] book of [the] generations of Adam. In [the] day of God's creating humankind, in [the] likeness of God he made him.

en.L: This [is] the book of the generations of Adam. In the day God created {{gender:humankind|man}}, in the likeness of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: This is the written account of Adam's family line. When God created {{gender:human beings|man}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them in the likeness of God.
en.R: This is the list of Adam's family. When God created {{gender:people|man}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them to be like God.

decisions.choice: the book of the generations: a written record of the family line
decisions.reason: "Book" means any written document, here a written list. "Generations" is the heading word of 2:4 and of each new section of Genesis; here it introduces Adam's descendants through Seth, down to Noah.

decisions.choice: Adam ... humankind: the same word as a name and as humankind
decisions.reason: The verse uses the word twice: first as the name of the first man, then, as in 1:26-27, for humankind. The list begins by going back to creation.

decisions.choice: in the likeness of God he made them: the words of 1:26-27
decisions.reason: The genealogy opens by repeating chapter 1: humankind made in God's likeness, male and female, blessed and named (verse 2). Whatever has happened in chapters 3-4, this is still what human beings are.

decisions.choice: humankind / human beings / people, and them; with the traditional setting, man and him
decisions.reason: As in 1:26-27: the word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive; the gender setting gives the traditional "man" and the Hebrew singular "him".

source.text: זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה בְּרָאָ֑ם וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָ֗ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמָם֙ אָדָ֔ם בְּי֖וֹם הִבָּֽרְאָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Male and female he created them, and he blessed them and called their name humankind in [the] day of their being created.

en.L: Male and female {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed them and called their name {{gender:Humankind|Man}} in the day they were created.
en.B: He created them male and female. He blessed them and named them {{gender:Humankind|Man}} when they were created.
en.R: He made them male and female. He blessed them and gave them the name {{gender:Human|Man}} on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them.

decisions.choice: called their name humankind: a name for man and woman together
decisions.reason: God gives the name adam to both, male and female together: it is the name of the human race, as well as of its first man (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Humankind (Human at Readable); with the traditional setting, Man
decisions.reason: The name given to both is the word for humankind (m1), capitalised as a name.

source.text: וַֽיְחִ֣י אָדָ֗ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּמְאַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בִּדְמוּת֖וֹ כְּצַלְמ֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵֽׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Adam thirty and a hundred year[s], and he fathered in his likeness, according to his image, and called his name Seth.

en.L: And Adam lived 130 years and fathered [a son] in his likeness, according to his image, and called his name Seth.
en.B: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image, and he named him Seth.
en.R: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son who was like him, and he named him Seth.

decisions.choice: in his likeness, according to his image: as Adam was made like God, Seth is like Adam
decisions.reason: The words of 1:26 return, in the other order. Adam passes on to his son the likeness he received from God: the image of God goes on in Adam's children (9:6).

decisions.choice: 130 years, as in the Hebrew text; the ages in this chapter differ in the ancient versions
decisions.reason: The ages at which the fathers have their sons differ between the Hebrew text, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint. The Septuagint often adds a hundred years (230 here), and the Samaritan text differs for Jared, Methuselah and Lamech. The Hebrew numbers are followed throughout.

decisions.choice: long lifespans: the ages given in the text
decisions.reason: The men of this list live for centuries, and the ages fall after the flood (11:10-26) to the length of a life in later times (Psalm 90:10). Other ancient lists, such as the Sumerian King List, give far larger numbers for the rulers before the flood. The text gives the numbers without comment.

decisions.choice: 130 years
decisions.reason: Hebrew often gives the smaller number first ("thirty and a hundred years"). English says the larger first and, by the style of this translation, writes numbers over ninety-nine as numerals.

decisions.choice: fathered [a son]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathered" with no object until the name; Literal brackets "a son".

source.text: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ יְמֵי־אָדָ֗ם אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־שֵׁ֔ת שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵאֹ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃

en.L: And the days of Adam after he fathered Seth were 800 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
en.B: After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
en.R: After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 more years. He had other sons and daughters too.

decisions.choice: sons and daughters: many other children, unnamed
decisions.reason: Each father in the list has other sons and daughters besides the one named. The list follows one line; these other children explain where the people of 4:14-17 came from.

decisions.reason: The words "and he died" close each life but one (verse 24), eight times in all. God's word in 2:17 and 3:19 has come true: however long they live, they die.

decisions.choice: walked with God: lived in close fellowship with God
decisions.reason: Where the formula says "lived", Enoch "walked with God". The verb form means to walk about, the form used of God walking in the garden (3:8); it is said again of Noah (6:9). It describes a life lived in God's company. The Septuagint translates it "pleased God", the wording Hebrews 11:5 follows.

decisions.choice: lived close to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

decisions.reason: Enoch's life is the shortest in the list, and the number equals the days in a solar year, perhaps a sign of a complete life. Unlike every other father in the list, he is not said to have died (verse 24).

decisions.choice: on earth
decisions.reason: Readable adds "on earth" to prepare for verse 24, where God takes Enoch.

decisions.reason: "He was not" breaks the refrain "and he died". The verb "took" is the one used when God takes Elijah up to heaven (2 Kings 2:3, 5, 9-10), and Hebrews 11:5 says Enoch "was taken up so that he did not see death". The text does not say where God took him.

source.text: וַיִּהְיוּ֙ כָּל־יְמֵ֣י מְתוּשֶׁ֔לַח תֵּ֤שַׁע וְשִׁשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And were all [the] days of Methuselah nine and sixty year[s] and nine hundred year[s], and he died.

en.L: And all the days of Methuselah were 969 years, and he died.
en.B: Altogether, Methuselah lived 969 years, and then he died.
en.R: Methuselah lived to be 969 years old, and then he died.

decisions.choice: 969 years: the longest life in the Bible
decisions.reason: Methuselah lives longest of all. By the numbers in the Hebrew text (verses 25, 28; 7:6), he dies in the year of the flood.

source.text: וַֽיְחִי־לֶ֕מֶךְ שְׁתַּ֧יִם וּשְׁמֹנִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּמְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד בֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Lamech two and eighty year[s] and a hundred year[s], and he fathered a son.

en.L: And Lamech lived 182 years and fathered a son.
en.B: When Lamech had lived 182 years, he had a son.
en.R: When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.

decisions.choice: Lamech: Noah's father, not the Lamech of 4:18-24
decisions.reason: This Lamech belongs to Seth's line. Where Cain's Lamech boasted of revenge (4:23-24), this one speaks of the hope of relief (verse 29).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֶת־שְׁמ֛וֹ נֹ֖חַ לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֞֠ה יְנַחֲמֵ֤נוּ מִֽמַּעֲשֵׂ֨נוּ֙ וּמֵעִצְּב֣וֹן יָדֵ֔ינוּ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽרְרָ֖הּ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called his name Noah, saying, this [one] will comfort us from our work and from [the] painful toil of our hands, from the ground which has cursed YHWH.

en.L: And he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will comfort us in our work and in the painful toil of our hands, from the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."
en.B: He named him Noah, saying, "He will bring us relief from our work and from the painful toil of our hands, caused by the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."
en.R: He named him Noah. He said, "This boy will give us rest from our hard work, from all the hard labor we must do on the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."

decisions.choice: Noah ... will comfort us: the name sounds like "rest" and "comfort"
decisions.reason: The name Noah (noach) sounds like the word for rest, and Lamech explains it with a verb of similar sound, "he will comfort us" (yenachamenu). The same verb returns in 6:6-7, where the LORD "regretted" that he had made humankind.

decisions.choice: painful toil ... the ground the LORD has cursed: the words of 3:17
decisions.reason: Lamech uses the words of God's judgment on the man: the cursed ground and painful toil (3:17). He hopes his son will bring relief from them. After the flood, Noah becomes a man of the soil who plants a vineyard (9:20), and God promises never again to curse the ground (8:21).

source.text: וַֽיְחִי־לֶ֗מֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־נֹ֔חַ חָמֵ֤שׁ וְתִשְׁעִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֹ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Lamech after his fathering Noah five and ninety year[s] and five hundred year[s], and he fathered sons and daughters.

en.L: And Lamech lived after he fathered Noah 595 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
en.B: After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
en.R: After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 more years. He had other sons and daughters too.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כָּל־יְמֵי־לֶ֔מֶךְ שֶׁ֤בַע וְשִׁבְעִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And were all [the] days of Lamech seven and seventy year[s] and seven hundred year[s], and he died.

en.L: And all the days of Lamech were 777 years, and he died.
en.B: Altogether, Lamech lived 777 years, and then he died.
en.R: Lamech lived to be 777 years old, and then he died.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־נֹ֕חַ בֶּן־חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֣וֹלֶד נֹ֔חַ אֶת־שֵׁ֖ם אֶת־חָ֥ם וְאֶת־יָֽפֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Noah a son of five hundred year[s], and fathered Noah Shem, Ham and Japheth.

en.L: And Noah was 500 years old, and Noah fathered Shem, Ham and Japheth.
en.B: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
en.R: When Noah was 500 years old, he had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

decisions.choice: a son of 500 years: 500 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives age as "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: Shem, Ham and Japheth: the usual order, not necessarily the order of birth
decisions.reason: The three sons are always listed in this order (6:10; 10:1), but 9:24 calls Ham the youngest, and 10:21 may call Japheth the eldest. The verse does not say they were born in one year; 500 is when Noah began to have sons. The line now opens out into the peoples of chapter 10.
